instructions.content: Ground every answer in sources: answers come exclusively from uploaded documents; never synthesise from general knowledge when querying a notebook.
Never guess notebook content: use Smart Add (query first) to discover what a notebook contains before labelling it.
Follow up until complete: check every answer for gaps and issue follow-ups before synthesising for the user.
When adding a notebook without full details, query the notebook first to discover its content, then use the discovered information to add it.
NEVER guess or use generic descriptions when adding a notebook; --description and --topics are REQUIRED.
ALWAYS run scripts through the run.py wrapper; NEVER execute the scripts directly, because they depend on the isolated .venv.
Check authentication status with auth_manager.py status before starting a session.
Authenticate with auth_manager.py setup; the browser MUST be visible for manual Google login, and the user must be told a browser window will open.
Manage the notebook library with notebook_manager.py (list, search, activate, add) so the right notebook is active before asking questions.
Use --markdown for responses containing code, lists or tables; add --log to save outputs.
Follow-up mechanism: when an answer ends with the 'Is that ALL you need to know?' prompt, STOP, ANALYZE, IDENTIFY GAPS, ASK FOLLOW-UP, REPEAT, then SYNTHESIZE before replying to the user.
Respect the 50 queries per day per Google account limit imposed by NotebookLM.
Do not run concurrent sessions: each query uses a fresh browser instance.
NEVER commit the data/ directory (library.json, auth_info.json, browser_state/); it is protected by .gitignore.
NEVER stop after the first answer when the request covers multiple points, because NotebookLM retrieves chunks, not full documents.
Keep questions specific and scoped; broad questions return fragmented answers.
When the browser crashes, recover with cleanup_manager.py --preserve-library so the notebook library is kept.
Do not use NotebookLM for general web search, LLM knowledge, data analysis or code generation; it is for document Q&A only.
Use descriptive names and topics so that library search is reliable.
